messages:
maya: Heads-up: starting a small project to 'capability striping' the runtime so ownership is clearer and we can retire a bunch of cross-cutting hacks. Not a big rip, iterative. Thoughts?

ravi: +1. Do you mean slice by capability (routing, enrichment, caching) or by tenant cohorts?

maya: capability-first: split session-router, enrichment, and cache-control into narrow tiles. Keep model-serving and billing global.

leo: main risk = losing batch efficiency and adding tail latency. We should preserve a batching shim in front of tiles initially.

tess: agree. also need a backwards-compatible surface. suggest a thin facade with header: X-Capability-Stripe: v1.

ravi: ops asks: how to migrate stateful pieces (cache, leases) without thrashing?

maya: plan: placement API + lease-based handoff. mark tenant migrating, warm new tile, switch, drain. observable via Console per-tenant.

leo: acceptance criteria: no >5% p95 on token path, per-tenant rollback in <10m, and no telemetry schema changes.

tess: tests: migration chaos, semantic diff on canonical prompts, and batch-size regression checks.

infra-bot: reminder: create staging deploy slot and tag deploys with "capability-striping".

maya: owners: ravi (placement & leases), leo (batching shim), tess (compat tests & runbook). I'll draft an RFC and post link here by EOD.

ravi: I'll prototype a tiny placement API and microbench next week.

leo: will mock batching shim and measure p50/p95.

tess: will prepare dashboards: tile.hit_rate, tile.batch.size, tile.queue.latency.p99.

maya: thanks. short sync tomorrow 10:00 PT to align on small scope and rollback knobs.
